headline: Gawdin scores twice as Rangers bury the Canucks
text:
Glenn Gawdin played eight minutes in Vancouver on Friday and scored his first two NHL goals in them. He was a Blues draft pick back in 2015 and has spent most of the years since in the AHL, and his two goals came a little over three minutes apart. That was the night in miniature: the Rangers scored five straight, beat the Canucks 5-1, and sent Vancouver to its seventh straight loss.

For a period, the Canucks were fine. Elias Pettersson tipped in a Zeev Buium shot at 12:13 for a 1-0 lead, and Brock Boeser's assist on it was the 500th point of his career, a milestone that deserved a better night around it. Gabe Perreault tied it late in the first. Then the second period got away from Vancouver: the Rangers out-chanced them 1.90 to 0.45 in expected goals, the quality of each team's chances. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored on the power play at 8:21, the goal that swung it most by our win probability (48% to 68%). Gawdin's first came unassisted at 13:00 after, as Daniel Wagner described it, Leevi Meriläinen put a pass into Filip Chytil's skates in Chytil's first game back. Alexis Lafrenière and Gawdin again made it 5-1 before the period was out.

J.T. Miller had two assists in his old building and, per Wagner's "I Watched This Game", went back to yelling at Pettersson, which keeps a feud alive that predates Miller's trade to New York. Miller was on the ice for 2.51 expected goals for and 0.99 against. Dylan Garand, the rookie who has carried the Rangers since Igor Shesterkin's season ended in October, stopped 27 of 28 and saved 1.9 goals more than his shots deserved.

The Rangers deserved to win this one 74% of the time by our count and are now 12-8-1. Vancouver is 3-17-1, and our playoff odds for them have reached zero in mid November. Chytil and Tom Willander are back, which helps, but a team that loses its second period this badly has bigger fixes to make than a lineup card.
